about: Maps archaic / Early Modern English (KJV) word forms to modern headwords, for search query expansion. Built by pipeline/build_lemma_bridge.py; do not edit by hand.

sources.Webster 1828: Noah Webster, An American Dictionary of the English Language (1828). Public domain. Parsed from github.com/DataWar/1828-dictionary (Vocabularium data/sources/webster1828.json.gz).
sources.Webster 1913: Webster's Revised Unabridged Dictionary (1913). Public domain (Vocabularium data/sources/webster1913.json.gz).
sources.Wordset: wordset/wordset-dictionary, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Vocabularium data/sources/wordset.json.gz). Used only to check that a rule-derived base is a real verb; no Wordset text is copied here.
sources.wordfreq: Top 50,000 wordfreq ranks, data CC BY-SA 4.0 (Vocabularium data/raw_ranks_50k.csv). Used only to decide what counts as a modern word; nothing is copied here.
sources.KJV: King James Version, this repo's data/greppable/kjv.tsv (pythonbible-kjv, built by pipeline/build_kjv.py). The text is public domain (Crown letters patent apply in the UK only).

rules.R1-eth: Third person singular -eth: strip it; the base must be a dictionary verb (walketh->walk, loveth->love, sinneth->sin, crieth->cry). Spelling tie-breaks: a one-syllable consonant-vowel-consonant base takes its silent e (hateth->hate, not hat); a doubled consonant is undone only if that leaves such a base (planneth->plan, falleth->fall); if two bases still fit, keep the one the text itself uses (singeth->sing, not singe), otherwise send it to review.
rules.R2-est: Second person singular -est: strip it; the base must be a dictionary verb, or a past tense that Webster 1828 lists under a verb (sayest->say, knewest->knew->know). If the base is also an adjective (superlative risk, e.g. "openest") the form must appear next to "thou" in the corpus.
rules.R3-edst: Second person singular past -edst: strip it; the base must be a dictionary verb (lovedst->love).
rules.R4-st: Second person singular -st on a modal or a past tense: canst->can, hadst->had->have, saidst->said->say. Modals are the closed class can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will, would, and keep their own form (couldest->could).
rules.R5-regular: Regular modern ending (-ed, -d, -ing, -s, -es) on an old SPELLING already in the bridge: same lemma (shewed->shew->show, enquired->enquire->inquire). Never on an old inflection (gates is not gat + -es).
rules.D-1828: Webster 1828: a form entry ("GAT, preterit tense of get."); a verb entry that lists its preterit/participle ("FORSAKE ... preterit tense forsook"), or marks one obsolete ("[forgat, obsolete]", "Holden is obsolete", "holp and holpen being obsolete"); "It is sometimes written shew, shewed, shewn"; "In lieu of this, establish is now always used". A form that is also a modern word needs a short plain entry, or it goes to review.
rules.D-1913: Webster 1913 sense opening "imp./p. p./2d pers. sing./3d pers. sing. of X" or "of X"; a one-word gloss that is itself a form of a verb (hath: "Has."); or "See X"/"Same as X" where the spellings differ by at most 2 letters, the form is rarer than X, and (if it is a modern word) every sense of it points to X. A modern word needs every 1913 sense to point to X, or a second-person form the text uses beside "thou" (wilt, art).
rules.P-pronoun: Second person pronouns (thee, thou, ye -> you; thy -> your; thine -> your, yours; thyself -> yourself), each quoted from Webster.
rules.A-reviewed: Decided by a person: data/lemma_bridge/review_decisions.csv records who, when and the verse that settled it. "bridge" rows enter the table ("bridge-modern" ones marked archaic: false); "keep-out" rows leave the review list as decided. Never edit the JSON by hand: add a row there and rebuild.
rules.C-chain: A lemma that is itself an archaic form is followed to its own lemma (sheweth->shew->show).

taught.quote: preterit tense and participle passive of teach. pronoun taut. [Latin doctus.]

thee.quote: The objective case of thou. See Thou.

thine.quote: A form of the possessive case of the pronoun thou, now superseded in common discourse by your

thou.quote: The nominative plural of the second person, of which thou is the singular. ... In common discourse and writing, you is exclusively used.

thought.quote: verb intransitive preterit tense and participle passive thought, pronoun thaut. [Latin duco.]

thrown.quote: verb transitive preterit tense threw; participle passive thrown. [Gr. to run; Latin trochilus.]

thy.quote: the more common form of thine, possessive case of thou

thyself.quote: An emphasized form of the personal pronoun of the second person

told.quote: verb transitive preterit tense and participle passive told. [Latin telum; Latin appello and peal, Latin pello.]

took.quote: verb transitive preterit tense took; participle passive taken. [Latin doceo. This word seems to be allied to think, for we say, I think a th

tossed.quote: verb transitive preterit tense and participle passive tossed or tost.

tost.quote: verb transitive preterit tense and participle passive tossed or tost.

tret.quote: 3d pers. sing. pres. of Tread, for treadeth.

trod.quote: verb intransitive tred. preterit tense trod; participle passive trod, troden. [Latin trudo.]

understood.quote: verb transitive preterit tense and participle passive understood. [under and stand. The sense is to support or hold in the mind.]

undertook.quote: verb transitive preterit tense undertook; participle passive undertaken. [under and take.]

underwent.quote: preterit tense of undergo. He underwent severe trials.

undid.quote: verb transitive preterit tense undid; participle passive undone.

undone.quote: Num 21:29 "thou art undone"; Matt 23:23 "leave the other undone"; Webster 1913: p. p. of Undo. Modern, archaic: false

unwound.quote: participle passive of wind. Wound off; untwisted.

upheld.quote: preterit tense and participle passive of uphold. Sustained; supported.

ware.quote: preterit tense of wear, obsolete It is now written wore.

wast.quote: past tense of the substantive verb, in the second person; as, thou wast

waxen.quote: verb intransitive preterit tense waxed.; participle passive waxed or waxen. [G., Latin , Gr.]

went.quote: verb intransitive preterit tense went; participle passive gone.

wept.quote: verb intransitive preterit tense and participle passive wept. Weeped, I believe is never used. [See Whoop. The primary sense is to cry out.]

wert.quote: The second person singular, indicative and subjunctive moods, imperfect tense, of the verb be. It is formed from were, with the ending -t, after the analogy of wast. Now used only in solemn or poetic

whilst.quote: Ps 141:10 "whilst that I withal escape"; Webster 1913: "While."

whipt.quote: participle passive of whip; sometimes used for whipped.

wist.quote: verb transitive preterit tense wist. To think; to suppose; to imagine.

withdrawn.quote: participle passive of withdraw. Recalled; taken back.

withheld.quote: preterit tense and participle passive of withhold.

won.quote: verb transitive preterit tense and participle passive won. [G.]

wook.quote: Woke. (woke is a form of wake)

wopen.quote: Wept. (wept is a form of weep)

wost.quote: 2d pers. sing. pres. of Wit, to know.

wot.quote: verb transitive preterit tense wot. [Latin , Gr.] To know.

wotest.quote: 2d pers. sing. pres. of Wit, to know.

woteth.quote: 3d pers. sing. pres. of Wit, to know.

would.quote: preterit tense of will, G., Latin

wound.quote: preterit tense and participle passive of wind.

wove.quote: verb transitive preterit tense wove; participle passive woven, wove. The regular form, weaved, is rarely or never used. [G., Gr.]

wringed.quote: verb transitive preterit tense and participle passive wringed and wrung. The latter is chiefly used.

wrote.quote: verb transitive preterit tense wrote.; participle passive writ, written. [Latin]

wrought.quote: preterit tense and participle passive of work. raut.

wrung.quote: verb transitive preterit tense and participle passive wringed and wrung. The latter is chiefly used.

wud.quote: preterit tense of will, G., Latin

ybe.quote: Been. (been is a form of be)

ydo.quote: Done. (done is a form of do)

ye.quote: The nominative plural of the second person, of which thou is the singular. ... In common discourse and writing, you is exclusively used.

yeven.quote: Given. (given is a form of give)

ygo.quote: Gone. (gone is a form of go)

ymaked.quote: Made. (made is a form of make)

yraft.quote: Bereft. (bereft is a form of bereave)
